issues.legal_issue: A developer’s construction of a flat under an agreement made with a purchaser before completion is a works contract to the extent of construction performed after that agreement.
material_facts: Developers entered into agreements with intended flat purchasers while construction was incomplete, and the agreements provided for construction and eventual transfer of the flats with an interest in the land.
The purchasers paid or were required to pay consideration, and goods used in construction were incorporated into the buildings and transferred to purchasers.
In the leading dispute, a developer also had a development agreement with a landowner under which the project was divided between them.
issues.conclusion: The construction activity is a works contract from the stage at which the developer enters into an agreement with the flat purchaser. The value addition to goods transferred after that agreement may be taxed. Construction completed before any purchaser agreement is not taxable on the basis of a later sale of the completed building.
issues.legal_principle: Article 366(29-A)(b), read with Entry 54 of List II, treats the transfer of property in goods involved in a works contract as a deemed sale, including goods incorporated into immovable property. Building contracts are works contracts, and a contract may combine construction with transfer of immovable property without losing its character as a works contract. The Court approved K. Raheja Development Corporation v. State of Karnataka; it relied on Builders’ Association of India v. Union of India, Gannon Dunkerley (II), State of U.P. v. P.N.C. Construction Co. Ltd., and State of A.P. v. Kone Elevators. The taxable construction activity begins when the developer contracts with the purchaser; goods incorporated before that point are not deemed sold to a purchaser who was not yet party to a construction contract.

predicates.construction_tax_appeal: The proceeding concerns a challenge to sales tax on goods used in constructing a building or flat.
predicates.developer_purchaser_agreement_before_com: The developer and purchaser agreed to the construction of the flat while construction was incomplete.
predicates.valuable_construction_consideration: The developer was entitled to valuable consideration for the construction undertaken for the purchaser.
predicates.construction_goods_transferred_to_purcha: Goods used in the construction were incorporated into the building and transferred to the purchaser in the completed property.

issues.definition: When a construction-tax appeal concerns a developer who agreed for valuable consideration to construct a flat for a purchaser before completion and transferred construction goods to that purchaser, the value of goods transferred through post-agreement construction may be taxed as a deemed sale.

issues.legal_issue: The dominant-intention test does not determine taxability of the goods component of a composite transaction covered by the constitutional rule for works contracts.
material_facts: The transactions combined construction of flats with their eventual sale and transfer of an interest in land.
The purchasers did not necessarily control the design, materials, or supervision of construction, and the ultimate transaction involved immovable property.
The taxing authorities sought to tax goods used in construction as part of those transactions.
issues.conclusion: The dominant-intention test does not apply to a composite transaction covered by Article 366(29-A); the goods component may be taxed if the transaction otherwise has the elements of a works contract.
issues.legal_principle: Article 366(29-A)(b) permits the divisible treatment of a works contract and deems the transfer of goods involved in its execution to be a sale. The dominant-nature test is inapplicable to transactions covered by Article 366(29-A), as explained in Associated Cement Companies Ltd. v. Commissioner of Customs and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. v. Union of India; Rainbow Colour Lab v. State of M.P. was overruled to the extent it required dominant intention for such transactions.

predicates.composite_construction_transaction: The transaction combines construction work with another element, such as transfer of a completed flat or an interest in land.
predicates.goods_involved_in_execution: Goods are used in carrying out the construction work.
predicates.property_in_goods_transferred: Property in the goods used in the work passes to another person, whether as goods or in another form.
predicates.state_sales_tax_case: The proceeding concerns state sales tax on the goods component of the transaction.

issues.definition: In a state sales-tax case involving a composite construction transaction in which goods are used and transferred, the dominant intention of the transaction does not determine whether the goods component is taxable.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory definition that includes agreements for building and construction may constitutionally reach transactions involving the transfer of goods in the execution of a works contract.
material_facts: The challenged statutory definition was amended to include agreements for building and construction for consideration.
The challenge concerned whether that definition could apply to construction transactions involving the transfer of goods to purchasers.
The Court construed the definition as reaching transactions within the constitutional understanding of a deemed sale in a works contract.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the amended definition was rejected; it is valid when construed as covering transactions that fall within the constitutional scope of a works contract and the transfer of goods involved in its execution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 366(29-A)(b) and Entry 54 of List II permit taxation of goods transferred in the execution of a works contract, but do not permit state legislation to expand the tax beyond those constitutional limits. The Court relied on its conclusion that K. Raheja Development Corporation v. State of Karnataka correctly stated the law and agreed with the Bombay High Court’s construction of the challenged definition.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_construction: The proceeding challenges the constitutionality of a statutory definition used to tax construction transactions.
predicates.definition_covers_building_agreements: The statutory definition includes agreements for building or construction for consideration.
predicates.goods_transferred_in_works_contract: The transactions covered by the definition involve transfer of goods in the execution of construction work.

issues.definition: A definition covering building agreements is valid when the challenged construction transactions involve goods transferred in the execution of a works contract and the definition remains within that scope.

issues.legal_issue: A method for valuing goods in a construction contract that also transfers land is valid only if it taxes the value of goods at incorporation and excludes the value of the land and immovable property.
material_facts: The challenged valuation rule applied to construction contracts in which both the constructed property and the underlying land or an interest in it were conveyed.
The rule calculated the goods value by deducting specified items, including a cost attributed to the land, from the agreement value.
The Court held that the tax measure must reflect the value of goods when incorporated into the works and must not tax the transfer of immovable property.
issues.conclusion: The valuation rule was sustained subject to being read down so that it taxes only the value of goods at the time of incorporation and does not tax land or the transfer of immovable property; the State was directed to bring clarity to the rule.
issues.legal_principle: Article 366(29-A)(b), read with Entry 54 of List II, allows tax on the goods element of a works contract but not on the transfer of immovable property. Gannon Dunkerley (II) establishes that the measure is the value of the goods at the time of incorporation. The Court also relied on the distinction between the measure and the charge of tax discussed in Union of India v. Bombay Tyre International Ltd.

predicates.valuation_rule_challenge: The proceeding challenges a rule used to calculate tax on construction contracts.
predicates.construction_contract_conveys_land: The construction contract provides for conveyance of the constructed property together with the underlying land or an interest in it.
predicates.goods_value_is_calculated_under_rule: The challenged rule prescribes a method for calculating the value of goods involved in the construction.

issues.definition: When a challenged valuation rule applies to a construction contract conveying land and prescribes a goods-value calculation, it is valid only if the calculation measures goods at incorporation and excludes land and immovable property.

issues.legal_issue: A clarificatory trade circular and an optional composition scheme do not require interference when they are consistent with the governing construction-tax rules.
material_facts: A trade circular clarified the tax treatment of construction transactions.
A notification allowed registered dealers to opt for a composition scheme.
The Court found no error in the High Court’s view of the circular and notification and noted that claims of double taxation could be addressed in individual assessments.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no ground to interfere with the High Court’s treatment of the circular and notification.
issues.legal_principle: The circular was clarificatory and the notification offered a composition option. Their operation remained subject to the governing rules on taxation of goods in construction contracts and to determination of any double-taxation claim in an individual assessment.

predicates.appeal_challenging_tax_guidance_or_compo: The proceeding challenges a trade circular or a notification concerning a tax option for registered dealers.
predicates.circular_is_clarificatory: The circular explains the administration’s understanding of the tax treatment rather than creating a separate taxable category.
predicates.composition_scheme_is_optional: The notification permits eligible dealers to choose a composition method.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges clarificatory tax guidance and an optional composition scheme, no interference is required on those facts.
